:::{#exm-entropy-rescaled-uniform}
#### Rescaling and shifting a uniform random variable

Let $X$ be [uniformly distributed](random-variables.qmd#def-uniform) between $0$ and $1$.
By @exm-entropy-uniform with $a = 1$, the [entropy](#def-entropy) of $X$ is $\entropyf{X} = \log 1 = 0$.

For a number $a > 0$, the [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) $aX$ is uniformly distributed between $0$ and $a$,
so @exm-entropy-uniform gives $\entropyf{aX} = \log a$.
That value matches @thm-entropy-scaling, which gives $\entropyf{aX} = \entropyf{X} + \log a = 0 + \log a$.

For a number $c$, the random variable $X + c$ is uniformly distributed between $c$ and $c + 1$.
Its [density](random-variables.qmd#def-pdf) is $1$ between $c$ and $c + 1$,
so its entropy is $-\int_c^{c+1} 1 \cdot \log 1 \, dx = 0 = \entropyf{X}$,
as @thm-entropy-shift states.
